summary: Christophe Vielle is an Indologist who taught Sandra Smets. He served as a professor of Sanskrit at KU Leuven (attested 2009) and as a professor at Université catholique de Louvain (attested 2013).

Christopher André Holmboe (1796–1882) specialized in linguistics, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Oslo (~1814–1818) and under Silvestre de Sacy and Caussin de Perceval (1821), later serving at Oslo as Reader (1822) and Professor of Oriental Languages (1828).

Christopher Byrne specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA under G. Victor Sōgen Hori and completed his PhD at McGill University (attested 2015) under doctoral supervisor Grace S. Fong and teacher Robin D. S. Yates.
Christopher D. Emms is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at McMaster University under doctoral supervisor Shayne Clarke (attested 2012).

Christopher D. Wallis specializes in Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Rochester, University of Oxford under Alexis Sanderson, and UC Berkeley (PhD, 2014) under Robert P. Goldman and Alexander von Rospatt, later serving as guest lecturer at Naropa University (attested 2020).

Christopher Framarin works in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Hawaii (2001) and a PhD from the University of New Mexico (2005), later becoming an associate professor at the University of Calgary (attested 2014).
Christopher Hatchell is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Virginia under the academic mentorship of David Germano.

Christopher I. Beckwith (b. 1945) works in Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Ohio State University (~1964–1968) and Indiana University (~1974–1984) under Helmut Hoffmann and Thubten Jigme Norbu, holding posts at Indiana University (1982, ~1986).

Christopher Ives (b. 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served as Assistant Professor of Religion at the University of Puget Sound (~1987–2001) and as professor and chair of religious studies at Stonehill College (~2001).

Christopher Jon Jensen works in religious studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Saskatchewan, Kyoto University, and McMaster University (PhD, 2018), where his doctoral supervisor was James A. Benn.

Christopher Kelley is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from Columbia University and founded the Columbia Society for Comparative Philosophy. He has taught at Columbia University, The New School, and Brooklyn College.

Christopher Key Chapple is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He held posts at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (1982), Stony Brook University (1983), and Loyola Marymount University as Doshi Professor (1998–2017).

Christopher Minkowski (b. 1953) works in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Harvard (~1973–1986) and held posts at Iowa (~1986–1988), Brown (~1988–1989), Cornell (~1989–2005), and Oxford and Balliol College as Boden Professor of Sanskrit (~2005–2019).
Christopher Pinney (b. 1959) is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Australian National University and at University College London (~1995).

Christopher S. George works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at Columbia University under Royal W. Weiler (1965), founded the American Institute of Buddhist Studies (1972), and was a professor at the Institute for Advanced Studies of World Religions (attested 1982).

Christopher S. Queen (b. 1945) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He served at Harvard University as Dean of Students for Continuing Education (~1989–2008) and Lecturer on Buddhism and World Religions (~1989–2017).
Chu-tsing Li (1920–2014) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Iowa (~1949–1955) and held a post at the University of Kansas (~1966–1990).

Chuan-ying Yen specializes in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. Yen studied at Harvard University (PhD attested 1986) under doctoral supervisor John M. Rosenfield, tutor Chu-tsing Li, and teacher John Hay.

Chun-fang Yu (b. 1938) works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Columbia University (~1965–1973), later holding faculty posts at Rutgers University (~1972–2001) and as Professor at Columbia University (~2001–2018).

Chun-min Yen specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. Yen earned a PhD at the University of Arizona (attested 2004) under doctoral supervisor Robert M. Gimello and teacher Todd Brown, also studying under traditional teachers Chanyun and Sheng Yen.
